sector: Consumer Discretionary - Restaurants (franchisor / restaurant real estate)
as_of_note: Latest reported fiscal period is Q2 2026 (quarter ended 2026-06-30, 10-Q filed 2026-08-07). Price and events (Investor Day 2026-09-23) are as of 2026-09-26. thesis_id uses the calendar quarter in which the thesis was written (Q3 2026).
refresh_note: Set to 2026-12-25 (90 days) as instructed, BUT McDonald's Q3 2026 results are expected in early November 2026 (Q3 2025 was reported 2025-11-05; the exact 2026 date is not confirmed in our sources). Re-check this thesis immediately after the Q3 print: U.S. comparable sales and guest counts are the swing factors, and the July 2026 U.S. comp was reportedly slightly negative.
business_summary: McDonald's is mostly a landlord and brand-licensor, not a burger cook. Of 46,028 restaurants at 2026-06-30, 44,016 (95.6%) are run by franchisees and only 2,012 by the company. Franchisees pay McDonald's rent plus a royalty that is a percentage of their sales; McDonald's generally owns or holds long-term leases on the land and building, so it collects rent on real estate it controls. In FY2025 total revenue was $26.885B: franchised revenues $16.548B (rent + royalties + initial fees), company-operated restaurant sales $9.690B, other $0.647B. The franchise stream is the profit engine: franchised margin was $13.930B on $16.548B of franchised revenue (84.2%), and franchised margins were ~90% of all restaurant-margin dollars. Because McDonald's books only fees (not the $139.4B of FY2025 Systemwide sales), the reported operating margin is very high (46.1% in FY2025). The thesis question in 2026 is whether a structurally superb royalty/real-estate model can re-ignite guest counts: U.S. comps slowed to +0.8% in Q2 2026 with negative guest counts, low-income traffic has reportedly fallen nearly double digits over two years, and management just committed ~$8.5B of franchisee 'partnering support' (rent relief + capital) through 2036 to fund the McDonald's > NEXT turnaround.

moat.type: Global brand + unmatched scale (46,028 restaurants, >70M customers/day, ~220M active loyalty members) + controlled prime real estate leased to franchisees + purchasing/marketing scale that individual competitors cannot match
moat.rationale: The moat is structural and has survived decades: McDonald's controls the land/buildings under most restaurants, so franchisees are locked into long-term leases (future minimum rent receivable from franchisees under operating leases was $31.45B at 2025-12-31 per the 10-K lease note). The brand, marketing fund and supply chain scale let it sell at price points small chains cannot match, and the franchise structure earns an 84% margin on franchised revenue. Company-reported after-tax ROIC was 20.3% in FY2025. We keep WIDE rather than narrow because the damage in 2025-2026 is to traffic/demand, not to the franchise/real-estate economics; but we flag that ROIC has drifted down from 25.2% (FY2023) to 21.8% (FY2024) to 20.3% (FY2025), low-income guest counts are falling, and the company now has to pay franchisees (rent relief) to fund reinvestment - a sign the system's economics are stretched. If U.S. guest counts keep falling through 2027 despite NEXT, we would downgrade to narrow.

quality.notes: revenue_growth_3y = compound annual growth FY2022 $23.183B -> FY2025 $26.885B (5.1%/yr, includes FX; constant-currency growth was lower, e.g. FY2025 +4% reported / +2% constant currency). TTM revenue to 2026-06-30 is $27.702B (FY2025 $26.885B - H1 2025 $12.799B + H1 2026 $13.616B). gross_margin: McDonald's does NOT report a 'gross profit' line. We use the closest analogue, total restaurant margins / total revenues = FY2025 $15.351B / $26.885B = 57.1% (restaurant margins include $1.7B of D&A). H1 2026 was 56.7% ($7.716B / $13.616B). roic = COMPANY-REPORTED after-tax ROIC from the FY2025 10-K (20.3%), not our own calculation; our cross-check (TTM operating income $12.805B x (1 - 21.4% TTM tax rate) = NOPAT ~$10.06B over debt $39.863B + equity -$1.023B - cash $0.822B = ~$38.0B) gives ~26% ex-leases and ~19% if the $14.73B of operating-lease liabilities are added to capital. net_debt_to_ebitda = (long-term debt $39.863B - cash $0.822B at 2026-06-30) / TTM EBITDA $15.071B (TTM operating income $12.805B + TTM D&A $2.266B) = 2.59x. Including operating-lease liabilities ($14.039B long-term + $0.690B current) it is ~3.57x (approximate: a strict lease-adjusted ratio would also add back rent to EBITDA). Shareholders' equity is NEGATIVE (-$1.023B at 2026-06-30) because decades of buybacks were debt-funded; this is a deliberate capital-structure choice, not a sign of losses. FCF = cash from operations - capital expenditures: FY2023 $9.612B - $2.357B; FY2024 $9.447B - $2.775B; FY2025 $10.551B - $3.365B; TTM Q2 2026 $11.347B - $3.586B. FY2025 dividends paid $5.115B = 71.2% of FCF; dividends + buybacks ($2.056B) = 99.8% of FCF.

valuation.method: pe + fcf_yield (equal-weighted average of the two bands, computed by code/valuation.py)
valuation.method_detail: P/E leg: TTM GAAP diluted EPS $12.31 (FY2025 $11.95 - H1 2025 $5.74 + H1 2026 $6.10) x 18 / 21 / 24 = $221.58 / $258.51 / $295.44. 18x = roughly the bottom of MCD's 10-year P/E range (low ~18.8x per GuruFocus): traffic keeps falling, NEXT rent relief compresses franchised revenue, EPS growth stalls. 21x base = ~19% below the ~25.9x 10-year median - we deliberately do NOT assume the old premium returns, because EPS growth has slowed to ~6% (H1 2026), U.S. guest counts are negative, balance-sheet leverage is ~2.6x and cash yields ~4%. 24x high = NEXT works, guest counts recover, and the market re-rates toward (still below) the historical median. FCF-yield leg: TTM FCF per diluted share $10.91 ($7.761B / 711.1M Q2 2026 diluted shares) at required yields 6.0% / 5.0% / 4.25% = $181.83 / $218.20 / $256.71. We demand MORE than the 5.0/4.2/3.5% used for net-cash mega-caps (AAPL, V) because MCD carries ~$39B of net debt and management has just pre-committed ~$5B of partnering support through 2030 that will weigh on FCF. At $236.53 the stock trades at 19.2x TTM EPS and a 4.61% TTM FCF yield; dividend yield on the $7.44 annual rate is 3.15%.
valuation.verdict: fair - price is essentially AT our base fair value (+0.8% margin of safety). Not a buy under our 12% minimum margin of safety; a 12% MoS entry would be ~$209.75 and the cautious 18% rule would be ~$195.45.
valuation.caveats: The reported TTM figures do NOT yet include the cost of the McDonald's > NEXT partnering support announced 2026-09-23 (~$8.5B through 2036, ~$5B through 2030, a mix of rent relief and capital support; the company guides ~$3B/yr baseline capex 2027-2030 plus $1.5-2B cumulative capital partnering). Rent relief directly reduces franchised revenue, the highest-margin line. We cannot yet split the $5B between P&L (rent relief) and capex, so we show a sensitivity below rather than guess. Management targets offset this with operating margin in the 'low-to-mid 50% range by 2030' and FCF conversion in the 'mid-to-high 80% range by 2030' - those are targets, not results, and we did not put them into the base case.

sensitivity_runs.label: NEXT cost fully hits P&L and FCF: ~$5B through 2030 spread over ~4.25 years = ~$1.18B/yr = $1.65/share pre-tax; EPS reduced by the after-tax $1.30 to $11.01, FCF/share reduced by $1.65 to $9.26; same 18/21/24x and 6.0/5.0/4.25% (an assumption-driven stress case, not a forecast)
Historical-premium case: TTM EPS $12.31 x 21/24/26x and FCF/share $10.91 at mega-cap yields 5.0/4.2/3.5% (what the stock would be worth if the old quality premium returned)

valuation.trend: Price $236.53 (2026-09-25 close) is below its 50-day average ($262.52) and far below its 200-day average ($291.83) on Alpaca daily closes; it closed at a new 52-week low. 52-week close range $236.53-$341.08 (high on 2026-02-27); down 30.7% from that high and -22.6% since the 2025-12-31 close ($305.60). Clear downtrend - the market is pricing a structural traffic problem.

conviction_rationale: 3 of 5: a world-class, filing-verified business model (84% franchised margins, ~$7.2-7.8B/yr FCF, 50 consecutive years of dividend increases) at a price that is merely fair, not cheap, with genuinely unresolved problems - U.S. guest counts negative, low-income traffic reportedly down nearly double digits for two years, a July 2026 U.S. comp reportedly slightly negative, and a new multi-year $8.5B reinvestment bill whose returns are unproven. Leverage (2.6x net debt/EBITDA, negative equity) leaves less room for error than AAPL/V. We would need either (a) evidence that NEXT is lifting U.S. guest counts or (b) a price near/below ~$210 before this becomes a 4.
bull_case: Royalty + real-estate engine: FY2025 franchised revenue $16.548B at an 84.2% margin; franchised margins are ~90% of restaurant-margin dollars. McDonald's collects a percentage of franchisee sales (FY2025 Systemwide sales $139.4B) without bearing most restaurant-level labor and food costs.
Contractual rent annuity: $31.45B of future minimum rent receivable from franchisees under operating leases at 2025-12-31 - long-dated cash flows that do not depend on this quarter's traffic.

Fundamentals are slowing, not collapsing: H1 2026 revenue +6% (+3% constant currency), operating income +7%, diluted EPS $6.10 (+6%); every segment had positive comparable sales in Q2 2026. The 30% price fall is far bigger than any earnings decline so far.
Cash machine: FCF $7.2B in FY2025 and $7.76B TTM; 50 consecutive years of dividend payments with an increase every year; current rate $1.86/quarter ($7.44/yr, ~3.15% yield at $236.53).

Scale advantages in the value war: >70M customers served daily, nearly 220M 90-day active loyalty users (+13%), loyalty-member Systemwide sales $40B TTM (+20%). No rival can spread marketing, tech (GenAI ArchIQ) and purchasing costs over 46,000 units.
Unit growth continues: ~2,600 gross openings planned for 2026 and net unit expansion contributing ~2.5% to 2026 Systemwide sales growth (and 'nearly 2.5%' in 2027).
Valuation has de-rated: 19.2x TTM EPS vs a ~25.9x 10-year median (aggregator figure) - if NEXT restores guest-count growth, the premium case values the shares at ~$278 base.
risks: TRAFFIC IS THE CORE RISK. U.S. comps slowed to +0.8% in Q2 2026 (from +2.5% in Q2 2025), driven by price/mix with NEGATIVE guest counts; press reports say U.S. comps turned slightly negative in July 2026 and the CEO said low-income traffic has fallen nearly double digits over ~two years and 'we're not expecting things to change.' Global comps slowed from +3.8% (Q2 2025) to +1.3% (Q2 2026).

Execution: management conceded on the Q2 call that it 'didn't execute at the level we needed'; the U.S. everyday-affordable-price menu was reportedly adopted by only ~60-65% of U.S. franchisees. The President of McDonald's USA (Joe Erlinger) was replaced on 2026-08-04.

The $8.5B NEXT partnering bill: ~$5B through 2030 of rent relief and capital support to franchisees. Rent relief directly cuts the highest-margin revenue line; press reports put the company's own payback at 5-6 years. The market sold the stock ~5% on the day (Alpaca close $250.36 on 9/22 -> $238.30 on 9/23). In our stress case, fair value falls to ~$208 base (-13.6% MoS).

Franchisee health: company-operated U.S. margins fell 14% in FY2025 and another 14% in H1 2026 on 'ongoing inflationary cost pressures' - franchisees face the same squeeze. The need for rent relief suggests franchisee cash flows are strained; a system-wide conflict or slower remodel investment would hurt comps.

Leverage: $39.9B of long-term debt vs $0.8B cash; net debt/EBITDA 2.59x (~3.6x including $14.7B of operating-lease liabilities); negative shareholders' equity (-$1.0B). Ratings BBB+/Baa1. Interest expense guided +4-6% in 2026. Dividends + buybacks consumed ~100% of FY2025 FCF, so extra NEXT spending likely slows buybacks or raises debt.
Secular demand headwinds: GLP-1 weight-loss drugs are cited by analysts as an early but real headwind to fast-food frequency; this is not quantified in any filing and we treat its size as unknown.

International softness: France and China cited as negative comps in Q2 2026; ~39% of debt is foreign-currency denominated and reported results swing with FX (FY2025 revenue +4% reported vs +2% constant currency).
Growth target slippage: the 50,000-restaurant goal was reportedly pushed from 2027 to 2028.
what_would_break_thesis: U.S. comparable sales negative for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026 was +0.8%; press reports July 2026 slightly negative) - the demand engine is failing, not just slowing.
Global comparable sales negative for two consecutive quarters outside a recognised recession (Q2 2026: +1.3%).

Franchised margins (franchised revenue less franchised occupancy) decline year-on-year in constant currency for two consecutive quarters - that would mean rent relief / franchisee distress is eating the royalty engine (Q2 2026: $3.713B, +3% constant currency).
Net debt to EBITDA (ex-leases) rises above 3.25x (2.59x at 2026-06-30), or S&P/Moody's downgrade the long-term rating below BBB/Baa2 (currently BBB+/Baa1).
Free cash flow below $6.0B in any full fiscal year (FY2025 $7.186B; TTM $7.761B), or dividends paid exceed free cash flow for a full year (FY2025: dividends were 71% of FCF).
Dividend cut or freeze (50 consecutive years of increases through FY2025).
Company-reported after-tax ROIC below 17% (FY2025 20.3%, down from 25.2% in FY2023).
The NEXT partnering commitment is raised materially above the announced ~$8.5B (or ~$5B through 2030), or operating margin guidance is cut below the 'mid-to-high 40%' 2026 range.
Any accounting red flag: restatement, material weakness, qualified audit opinion, or an unexplained auditor change.
sell_triggers: U.S. comparable sales negative for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026: +0.8%).
Global comparable sales negative for two consecutive quarters outside a recession (Q2 2026: +1.3%).
Franchised margins down YoY in constant currency for two consecutive quarters (Q2 2026: +3% cc).
Net debt/EBITDA (ex-leases) above 3.25x (now 2.59x) or a credit downgrade below BBB/Baa2.
Full-year FCF below $6.0B (FY2025 $7.186B), or dividends exceed FCF for a full year.
NEXT partnering support raised materially above ~$8.5B, or 2026 operating-margin guidance cut below mid-to-high 40%.
Any accounting red flag (restatement, material weakness, qualified opinion).
catalysts: Q3 2026 results, expected early November 2026 (Q3 2025 was reported 2025-11-05; 2026 date not yet confirmed in our sources). The key numbers: U.S. comparable sales and guest counts (was July's reported negative comp a blip?), franchised margin growth, and any quantification of NEXT costs for 2027.
'Make It Golden' system-wide customer-experience program launching 2026-10-05 (Founder's Day) - early read on whether hospitality/food-quality investments move traffic.
Q4 2026 results and 2027 guidance (~February 2027): first guidance year that includes NEXT partnering support; watch operating margin and capex vs the ~$3B/yr baseline target.
Annual dividend increase decision (last raised 5% to $1.86/quarter in Q4 2025) - the size of the Q4 2026 raise is a signal of management's FCF confidence.
Downside catalyst: a consumer recession would hit the low-income customer hardest; upside catalyst: easing cost-of-living pressure or a successful value platform reset restoring guest counts.
